login.name: EcoFlow Login (skip if you already have your user ID)
login.description: After you click Submit with your login information filled in, your EcoFlow User ID will be automatically populated and this form will clear itself. Only your user ID is required so you will not be able to proceed to the next page unless this section is empty.

data_description.region: Pick the EcoFlow API host matching your account. Auto uses api.ecoflow.com for email and api-cn for phone numbers. Your account may live on a different host than your actual geographic region, so if you receive an "Account does not exist" message, try selecting the host explicitly.

log_options.description: Detailed logging options. Most of these will flood your logs, so avoid leaving them enabled for long periods.

data.log_masked: Mask sensitive information (useful when sharing logs publicly)
data.log_connection: Log device connection requests and responses
data.log_bleak: Enable bleak debug log level (not masked and not filtered to this device)

advanced_connection_options.name: Advanced connection options
advanced_connection_options.description: These options affect the Bluetooth connection behavior. Only change them if you are experiencing connectivity issues.

data_description.connection_timeout: Number of seconds to wait for the device to connect and authenticate.
data_description.connection_delay: Number of seconds to wait before connecting when another EcoFlow device has just connected. Home Assistant picks which Bluetooth proxy each connection goes through and penalizes proxies that are already busy connecting, so devices coming up at the same moment can end up on a more distant proxy for the rest of the session. Spacing them out gives each device a better chance of being connected through the proxy closest to it. A device that is not coming up alongside another is never delayed. Set to 0 to disable this for the device.
data_description.preferred_proxy: Connect this device through a particular Bluetooth adapter or proxy when possible, for example the one sitting next to it. Home Assistant chooses the path itself and cannot be told to use a specific one, so the integration instead waits until the proxy you pick is the one Home Assistant would choose anyway, and connects at that moment. A proxy whose signal is weaker than another may therefore never be chosen. The list is taken when this page opens and only holds adapters and proxies that are online right now, so if one is missing, bring it back online and reopen this page. Leave this on "Any available proxy" unless a device keeps connecting through the wrong one.
data_description.preferred_proxy_timeout: Number of seconds to wait for the preferred proxy before connecting through whatever proxy is available. A proxy that is already online is usually picked straight away, so this only comes into play when it is still starting up - after restarting Home Assistant, a proxy can take a while to come back, and the device stays disconnected until it does or this runs out. Set to 0 to connect immediately through whichever proxy is best at that moment.
data_description.bluez_start_notify: Try enabling this if you experience frequent disconnects when multiple BLE devices are connected, or if you see `AcquireNotify: Read error` / `Unexpected EOF on notification file handle` in your logs.

device_options.name: Device options
device_options.description: Advanced options specific to this device model. Only change these if you know what you are doing.

data_description.unlock_ac_charging_minimum: Allows setting the AC charging speed below the minimum the EcoFlow app enforces. 1 W stops the device drawing from the grid without unplugging it, which is what solar-surplus automations need; charging that slowly is less efficient and may generate additional heat.
data_description.unlock_dc_charging_minimum:
⚠️ WARNING: this may damage your device. The EcoFlow app limits are likely there for a reason, and running the DC input below them for long periods can wear its components; damage caused this way may not be covered by warranty. Use at your own risk.

Allows setting the DC charging speed below the minimum the EcoFlow app enforces, down to 0 A. 0 A is not off: the device can still draw a small current from the input. The value caps the current drawn from the DC input, so a lower one keeps the device within what a weak source can give - a fuse-limited car socket, a small supply or a single panel - instead of stalling it by asking for more.

diagnostics_options.name: Diagnostics
diagnostics_options.description: Configure diagnostics data collection and encryption.

data_description.diagnostics_on_exception: When enabled, packets are collected from the start of each connection attempt. If a connection error occurs, collected data is automatically saved to disk for debugging.
data_description.collect_packets:
Enabling this option will start storing packets for diagnostics info - wait a minute after you enable this option before downloading diagnostics info and don't forget to turn it off.
Some devices may contain identifying information in their messages such as your exact location, make sure encryption is enabled before sharing.
data_description.diagnostics_encrypt: When enabled, sensitive diagnostics data (packets, session keys, manufacturer data) is encrypted before being included in the diagnostics download. Disable only if you need raw data for local debugging.

charging_minimum_applied.title: Charging controls on {device_name} now stop at the EcoFlow app's minimum unless you unlock it in the device options
charging_minimum_applied.description:
The AC and DC charging controls now refuse values below the minimum the EcoFlow app enforces, so an automation that sets a lower value will fail with an out-of-range error.

⚠️ WARNING: going below these minimums may damage your device. EcoFlow likely set them for a reason, running below them for long periods can wear its components, and damage caused this way may not be covered by warranty. Only unlock them if you accept that risk.

To keep setting values below the minimum, turn on the matching option under Configure for this device.

The minimums for this device are {minimums}.
